artists.biography: Joan Jett (born Joan Marie Larkin; September 22, 1958) is an American rock guitarist, singer, songwriter, producer and occasional actress. She started her career as a founding member of The Runaways but is best known for her work with Joan Jett & the Blackhearts, including their hit cover "I Love Rock 'n' Roll", which was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 from March 20 to May 1, 1982, as well as for their other popular recordings including "Crimson and Clover", "I Hate Myself for Loving You", "Do You Want to Touch Me", "Light of Day", "Love Is All Around" and "Bad Reputation". She has three albums that have been certified Platinum or Gold, and she has been referred to as the "Queen of Rock 'n' Roll" many times during her career.

perplexity.description:
Bad Reputation is Joan Jett's debut solo studio album, originally released independently in May 1980 following the dissolution of her band The Runaways. After major record labels rejected the project, Jett and producer Laguna self-funded the initial pressing, which was sold directly to concert-goers and record stores. The album's success prompted a worldwide re-release through Boardwalk Records on January 23, 1981, under the new title that referenced the controversial reputation Jett had acquired from her work with The Runaways.

The album showcases a straightforward rock sound rooted in punk and hard rock aesthetics. Jett contributed songwriting to only four of the twelve tracks, drawing from a mix of original compositions and covers that demonstrated her ability to command material across different styles. The title track, "Bad Reputation," emerged as one of her signature songs and would later be recognized as the 29th best hard rock song of all time by VH1 in 2009, the highest-ranked song by a woman on that list. Five singles were released from the album, establishing Jett's commercial viability as a solo artist.

The album received positive critical reception and reached number 51 on the Billboard 200, establishing Jett as a significant figure in rock music. Its commercial performance validated her independent approach and paved the way for her subsequent success, particularly with the formation of Joan Jett & the Blackhearts and the massive popularity of her 1982 follow-up album I Love Rock 'n' Roll. The 1980 debut remains a foundational work in Jett's career and an important entry point in the history of women in rock and roll.
